| [THEORY-134](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-134.md) v3 | Viability kernel is the part that can persist | Aubin's viability theory, read in his 1999 mini-course notes [LIT-714](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-714.md). Given dynamics and a set K of required states, K is viable if some evolution from each state stays in K and invariant if every one does. Nagumo's theorem reduces viability to a tangency condition. The viability kernel is the largest viable subset of K; from outside it every evolution exits K. The notes do not compare viability with stability; that contrast is a further step. | Active |
| [THEORY-771](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-771.md) v5 | Below ε_c, contracting slow–fast stays O(ε) close | Bousquet and Slotine (arXiv 2015), [LIT-1292](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1292.md), read in [NOTE-1025](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1025.md). It gives Simon's near-decomposability the rate in ε that [THEORY-661](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-661.md)'s open statement lacks: first order, for trajectory error, uniform in time, under contraction of the modules and of the reduced slow system, with an explicit, sufficient ceiling on ε. Deterministic. It bounds how far the states are from the reduced description, not how much information the rest of the system sends into the slow variables, and it takes the slow coordinates as given. | Active |
| [THEORY-773](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md) v2 | Slow-manifold error is O(ε) under contraction | Del Vecchio and Slotine (IEEE TAC 2013), [LIT-1295](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1295.md), read in [NOTE-1020](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1020.md), with their Theorem 3's hypothesis corrected. A global, uniform-in-time, first-order bound on the error of the quasi-steady-state reduction, with every constant explicit and no requirement that ε be small. The reduction is Markovian: eliminating a fast, contracting variable costs O(ε) in trajectory error for all time, so no memory term is needed to that order. Constant metrics, deterministic, and the bound d on how fast the manifold moves is needed along the trajectory. | Active |

| [THEORY-2043](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2043.md) v2 | Contraction gives exponential convergence | From the reading of [LIT-2831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2831.md) in [NOTE-2088](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2088.md). Lohmiller, Slotine (1998), Automatica 34(6), DOI 10.1016/S0005-1098(98)00019-3, read from the authors' final manuscript (NSL-961001, December 1997) on the MIT Nonlinear Systems Laboratory site. It founds contraction analysis. If the generalized Jacobian F = (Θ̇ + Θ ∂f/∂x)Θ⁻¹ is uniformly negative definite in a metric M = ΘᵀΘ, all trajectories in a ball inside the region converge exponentially to one another, so initial conditions are forgotten. Conversely, every exponentially convergent system is contracting in some metric, and contraction survives parallel, skew- symmetric feedback and hierarchical combination, the last offered as a common frame for singular perturbations. Here because A29 grounded selective contraction in it; it is not the source of partial contraction toward invariant manifolds (that is Wang and Slotine 2005, not held), only of two remarks on convergence on a subspace. [THEORY-773](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md)'s disturbance lemma rests on its eq. (15). Read in its NOTE. | Proposed |

The partial contraction the reading of Lohmiller and Slotine found missing. Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2221](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2221.md) | Regulation is second-order control | Bich, Mossio, Ruiz-Mirazo and Moreno, read in [NOTE-2310](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2310.md) (Read).
